question_type: argmax month of a yield spread over a decade from one pinned issue, with a question-defined output encoding (month*100 + calendar year); the table's year labels were lost in OCR
decisive_step: Recovering the years of the June-1970 AY-1 monthly block (treasury_bulletin_1970_06.txt:4949-4984: 36 month rows x 4 column groups, year-label row lost in OCR): each group stacks 3 consecutive years and the groups start 1959/1962/1965/1968, anchored from a sibling printing that kept the year row (reference worklog.md Step 4: 1970_03:4789 and 1971_06 Jan rows identical to the June rows; internal anchor: group 4's third block stops at May, matching a June-1970 issue). With that mapping the argmax over Jan 1960-Dec 1969 is unambiguous although the top two months differ only in the second decimal (worklog Step 5; calc.py:20-31, 36) and the answer is month*100 + the four-digit year (calc.py:37). Both wrong cells had the right table and the right cells on screen: b mis-decoded which cell its argmax index pointed at (an out-of-window 1970 month), c encoded the year with two digits.

a.path_summary: find_tables 'Aa' --years 1970 (a[6]) found AY-1 at 1970_06:4946. show_table --long --grep 196 (a[8]) returned only the weekly rows, but its NOTES said 137 month rows carry no year and listed SIBLINGS (1970_07:4447 first). It read the June table raw (a[10]) and the July sibling raw (a[12]), whose year row survived, then parsed lines 4949-4984 in calc with year = group base + row//12, filtered 1960-1969 and ranked (spread, year, month) tuples (a[14]-[26], after three script fixes). It encoded month*100 + four-digit year by hand at a[27].

first_divergence.what_it_did: Acted on the SIBLINGS note, anchored the group years from the July printing and kept the June values (pinned issue).
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: Same as the reference (worklog Step 4), which used 1970_03 and 1971_06 as anchors.

tool_use.friction: a[8] --grep 196 cannot select Y? month rows (their filled period has no year), so only weekly rows matched; a[14] calc runs in the workspace, so the bare corpus filename raised FileNotFoundError; a[16],[22],[24] three iterations to handle footnote marks ('4/') and 'nan' cells, a[22] output truncated; the final encoding was computed in THINK, not in calc.

a.text_use: a[13] 'User explicitly exact publication June 1970, so use that issue, not latest' (the latest-printing item's exception); a[13] 'Need calculate with calc'. The year anchoring came from the tool NOTE at a[8], not from the text.

b.path_summary: find_tables with 'yield spread' wording gave 0 hits (b[4]); rg over the corpus (b[6]-[11]) located AY-1; sed (b[13]) and show_table --raw (b[15], which prints no NOTES) showed the year-less block. At b[16] it reasoned the 4-groups x 3-stacked-years layout and the 1959..1970 mapping correctly. Its calc (b[17]) flattened the cells row-major (4 groups per row) and printed the argmax as a flat index; at b[18] it decoded that index group-major (index//36 = group) as the last month of group 3, whereas row-major it is the third month of group 4's third block, a 1970 cell outside the window. It re-ran the identical calc three times (b[17],[19],[21]) until a loop note, confirmed the year mapping with printings (b[25]), submitted with a two-digit year (b[27]), was told to recompute in calc (recompute_final), ran the encoding with the four-digit year (b[29]) and resubmitted (b[31]).

first_divergence.what_it_did: Decoded the argmax flat index as 'group 3, last row' although its list was built row-major (row = index//4, group = index%4), so the chosen cell was a 1970 month mislabelled as an in-window month; it also never filtered to 1960-1969.
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: a[26] carried (year, month) inside every tuple and filtered the window before taking the max; the reference asserted 120 in-window months (calc.py:33).

tool_use.friction: b[4] 0 hits for 'yield spread' wording; b[8] rg with a bare filename (not found); b[15] --raw shows no NOTES/SIBLINGS/Y? warnings; b[17]-[21] identical calc three times (loop); b[25] printings output cut at 8000 bytes (328 cells; it still showed the year mapping).

b.harness_use: loop_guard note at call 12 after three identical calcs broke the repetition (b then ran sed and printings) but did not point at the unverified decode step. Gate round 1 (checks/001.json): recompute_final on the first submit, which was hand-encoded with a two-digit year and not a calc output; b then ran the encoding in calc with the four-digit year and resubmitted (checks/002.json accepted). The gate fixed the encoding slip but was blind to the period error because the cells were parsed inside calc from the raw file (no cell bindings; period_match silent). The answer changed between submits; both wrong.

c.path_summary: Four find_tables queries (c[6]-[12]) reached AY-1. show_table --long --from-row 1 (c[15]) hid the NOTES ('4 (shown on the first page)'); sed raw (c[17]) and paged views (c[20],[22]) with Y?1/Y?2 periods were read as one year per panel (1959-1963) (c[21],[23]); it then hunted for a chart or a longer table (c[24]-[33]). Opening the Nov-1970 printing (c[35],[42]), whose year labels survived, gave it labelled rows; it re-read the June panels (c[41], still off by a year but harmless), hand-typed seven late-1969 months from the Nov-1970 printing into calc, found the same month as the reference, and encoded 11*100 + a two-digit year inside calc (c[44]); answered at c[46].

first_divergence.what_it_did: Encoded the answer as month*100 + the two-digit year inside calc although the question says 'add it to the corresponding calendar year'; the month it picked is the reference's. (Earlier CELL_SELECTION detours at c[21]-[41] were self-corrected and did not change the pick; values were read from the Nov-1970 printing rather than the pinned June issue, but they are identical.)
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: a[27] and the reference (calc.py:37) added the four-digit calendar year.

c.text_use: c[19] SAY 'using the table's full row structure and later explicit printings to map each month to its year' (period item, partially); c[43] 'Let's calc' (calc item); c[36] reasoned about 'Use data from bulletin published in June 1970' (pinned-issue exception). No text item covered output encodings.

smallest_change.change: Add to the Working advice: 'Encoded answers: when the question defines the answer by a formula (for example "multiply the month by 100 and add it to the calendar year"), evaluate that formula in calc with the full values the question names: a calendar year is four digits (1969, not 69), a month is 1-12. Check that the result has the digit count the formula implies before answering.'
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: no: a already encoded this way; the sentence only applies when the question spells out a formula.

alternatives.change: show_table anchors Y? years automatically from the SIBLINGS printing it already finds (otables.py:1734 siblings(); the July sibling's year row at 1970_07:4450 gives the group start years and its first data rows are identical to the June rows) and prints the anchored period in every view (rows, --long, --raw), e.g. `4971  4  1969-11~  Nov   <v1>  <v2>  <v3>  YEAR_FROM_SIBLING 1970_07:4450`, with one NOTE `years anchored from sibling 1970_07:4450: groups start 1959/1962/1965/1968, 3 stacked years per group`; and print the NOTES block on every page and in --raw, not only at --from-row 0 (otables.py:1976-1979) and never in raw mode (otables.py:1887).
alternatives.why_not_first: This is the fix for the structural failure that sank all three v8 arms and drove c's detour, and both v9 wrong cells viewed the table in a mode that hid the SIBLINGS note (b[15] --raw, c[15] --from-row 1). But neither v9 cell was killed by the year mapping: b had the right mapping and mis-decoded its own flat index; c had the right month. Strongly recommended for v10 anyway: with labelled periods in the tool output neither cell needs a hand-rolled parser, and the period of every candidate is visible.

alternatives.change: Argmax provenance: when the final calc's output is a max/argmax over rows parsed from a file, the gate requires the printed winner to carry a period (a YYYY-MM or (year, month) next to the max value) and that period to lie in the question's window; otherwise finding: 'Your argmax carries no period; print (period, value) tuples and take the max of the in-window rows.'
alternatives.why_not_first: Needs a calc-output convention; b[17] printed bare flat indices, so the rule would have fired, but the harness cannot know what index 107 denotes; it is a nudge, not a fix.

alternatives.change: Encoding range check: when the question matches 'multiply ... by 100 ... add ... year', the submitted value must equal m*100 + y with y a four-digit year taken from the calc that produced it; otherwise finding 'The question adds a calendar year (four digits); your calc added a two-digit year.'
alternatives.why_not_first: Question-pattern specific; the TEXT sentence delivers the same knowledge before the mistake is typed, and recompute_final already forces the encoding into calc where it can be seen.

fix.why_not_text: n/a (the fix is TEXT). Evidence that text can work here: a's text had no encoding item and c's error was a deliberate two-digit year typed into calc at c[44]; the word 'year' was read as two digits, which one explicit sentence removes. Residual risk is the usual one at temperature 1: the sentence may not be read.

notes: (1) NOTES are printed only on the --from-row 0 page (otables.py:1976-1979) and never in --raw mode (raw branch at otables.py:1887 returns raw lines only). The 'anchor the years from a sibling printing ... never by guessing' note (otables.py:1259) and the SIBLINGS list (otables.py:1974) are exactly what separated a from b and c, and both wrong cells used a view that hid them (b[15] --raw, c[15] --from-row 1). Cheapest tool change: always print the NOTES block. (2) --grep matches the filled period, the raw label or the section (otables.py:1984); Y? rows have no year in their period, so --grep 196 (a[8]) can never select them; the tool should say so, or grep the anchored period once (alternative 1) exists. (3) --long on a 4-panel table lists every cell as a row (163 'rows'), so paging at 8000 bytes shows ~30 cells (c[15]); the ROWS view without --long is about 4x denser (c[20]). (4) calc runs in the workspace, so a bare corpus filename fails (a[14]); README could state that the absolute corpus path is required, or calc could export a CORPUS env var. (5) Frequency: the output encoding was mis-evaluated in 5 of the 6 wrong runs on this question across v8 (3 arms: digit concatenation x2, year-first) and v9 (b's first submit and c: two-digit year). recompute_final caught b's only because it was hand-computed; once typed into calc (c) no rule sees it. (6) b's loop (identical calc x3, b[17]-[21]) came from re-reasoning the same mapping; the loop note ended it, but the actor never re-examined the decode step, which is where the error was. (7) The top two months differ by 0.01 in spread (reference calc.py asserts no tie), so any OCR slip in one cell flips the month; the reference cross-checked both cells in ten issues (worklog Step 6); no v9 cell did.
